text:
The point of the study is to find out whether the new drug changes mitochondrial function.

A. 5,5′,6,6′-Tetrachloro-1,1′,3,3′-tetra­ethyl­benz­imidazolyl­carbocyanine iodide (JC-1) reports the mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm) by a ratiometric fluorescence shift; flow-cytometric JC-1 measurements directly monitor mitochondrial health.  →  Useful.

B. The firefly luciferase/luciferin system needs ATP to make light. Cytosolic ATP is produced mainly in mitochondria, so a fall or rise in light output tells you whether total cellular ATP production (and therefore mitochondrial output) is altered.  →  Potentially useful.

C. Mito-RTP (a rhodamine-based mitochondria-targeted probe) stains active mitochondria; confocal microscopy can reveal changes in mitochondrial number, morphology or membrane potential.  →  Useful.

D. After differential centrifugation you have a crude mitochondrial pellet lacking the plasma-membrane glucose transporters. A “Glucose Uptake Colorimetric Assay” measures how intact cells import glucose; isolated mitochondria neither take up extracellular glucose nor use the plasma-membrane transporters assayed by the kit. Doing this assay on a mitochondrial fraction can therefore tell you nothing about mitochondrial function or about the drug’s effect on mitochondria.  →  Not useful.

Hence the only experiment that will not help you learn about the drug’s mitochondrial effects is option D.

Answer: D
